Ethical Hacking

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We meet the people on the front lines of cyber security, the ethical hackers.

Unique Selling Point:
As security leaks, large scale hacking attacks and digital crimes become an ever increasing reality, governments and big business face an ongoing battle in cyber security. The need has given rise to a new kind of IT specialist - the ethical hacker. A culture born from counter culture, ethical hackers are literally paid to penetrate and exploit IT based systems.

Further information:
We will be speaking to several experts in the field to get an inside look at the world of ethical hacking. To keep things interesting we will show examples of what hackers are capable of ie: hacking a person's phone and their instagram account and taking over a desktop computer and retrieving info from it, hacking a phone and switching on and recording from its camera. All of the above will be done on the experts devices with full permission from the people involved.

Mr. Angus Clarke Ethical Hacker PWC

Press Release:


Hacking a Hacker
Is your business safe from a malicious online attack? Working on the premise of ‘it takes a thief to catch a thief’ a snowballing domain of hackers—of the ethical kind—are increasingly being paid to systematically infiltrate networks and expose vulnerabilities before they become a real problem. These so-called white-hats show Carte Blanche just how naive consumers and businesses could be prone to cyber attack and what you should know to stay safe.


Script:


Voice
Cyberspace. A parallel universe made up of bits and bytes that few of us fully understand. But as our daily lives become ever more reliant on the Internet, we are increasingly exposed to cyber crime and the hackers who perpetrate it.

Devi Link
We’ve all heard about hackers and their criminal exploits where they set out to steal information and turn it into cash

Voice
To combat the threat is a growing worldwide group of cyber security professionals known as ethical hackers.

Sound Up Mixo Ngoveni
It’s the good hacking. I’ll give you an example. Company A has just built a system now, they would hire a hacker, an ethical hacker, to go and hack into their system to test if their system is really strong.

Voice
Ethical hackers, or “whitehats” are really a group of computer security specialists who probe weak spots in digital systems. Governments and companies pay them for these services, so that they can fix any problems before “blackhats”, or criminal hackers, can exploit them. IT specialist and tech entrepreneur Mixo Ngoveni says ethical hackers need to be able to think like their criminal counterparts.

Sound Up Mixo
I mean what better person to hack into a system then a hacker. That way he can actually say: “no, there are problems here” because he understands and he thinks like a hacker.

Voice
Dominic White is the chief technology officer at Sensepost, a cyber security firm, and one of the country’s leading whitehats. He says he was fascinated by all things hacking from an early age.

Sound Up Dominic
There was a group of friends, we had an agreement that we were all allowed to hack each other as long as we told each other how we did it. And I remember once, you know because we didn’t actually have the technical skills, I was hanging outside my friend’s window, waiting for him to go to the toilet so that I could go in and load some software on his machine so I could get his password.


Voice
At university Dominic read a book on cyber security that changed his life and career choice forever.

Sound Up Dominic
And I remember I read a book called Secrets and Lies by a famous cryptographer named Bruce Schneier and it was at that point that I realised that this could be a job rather than a way to got to prison.

Voice
Dominic agreed to let Chris Le Roy, a penetration tester at Sensepost, give us a practical example of a hacker’s skills. What you are about to see is completely real, and although we are not going to show you every step in the process, none of it was faked.

Sound Up Chris
Devi: So what exactly are we going to do?

Chris: So what we have here is a mobile device, and we are going to trick this mobile device into connecting to our wireless network, which will then allow us to trick the device into installing my malicious application, which will then allow us to control the webcam and the microphone of the device.

Voice
In this example, the cellphone’s wifi is on, just like many of our smartphone’s usually are. When wifi is switched on, the phone is constantly searching for wifi networks it has connected to previously. In a matter of seconds, Chris convinces the phone his wifi network is one of the networks the phone has connected to before.

Sound Up Chris
For example Always On. If you’re at the BP you can connect to it, at a shopping mall or an airport. If your phone has connected to that previously, it will automatically go and connect to that. So the device is looking for the Always On network. We are going to say yes we are always on, connect to us. What that will then allow us to do is to trick the user into navigating to websites that are under our control.

Voice
The phone we used had the latest antivirus software installed, but that didn’t stop Chris.

Sound Up Chris
That’s because I’ve made the application look legitimate, and I know what the anti-virus is looking for.


Voice
So while the phone’s user unknowingly surfs the web, Chris can install his malware on the device in a variety of ways. Once the malware, which is essentially a virus, is installed on the phone, Chris can access a lot of the smart device’s features. If he were to install a keystroke logger on your phone for example, he would be able to see every letter you ever typed into the phone, including email and banking passwords…

Sound Up Chris
Chris: So I’m accessing your selfie camera. And there we go.

Devi: You’ve got me on video?

Chris: Yes

Devi: On your laptop?

Chris: On my laptop.

Devi: I have no idea though?

Chris: There’s no alerts. You can go onto Google now if you wanted, you can use the phone in any way.

Devi: This is scary.

Voice
Recording the audio from the phone’s microphone was just as simple.

Sound Up Chris
Chris: And I want to record the microphone for 5 seconds, and what that means now is that what I am saying now is being recorded and sent back. And if I now go on my machine and play that audio: SOUND UP AUDIO PLAYBACK “and what that means now is that what I am saying now”

Devi: Ok, and you can change that duration to make it even longer?

Chris: Absolutely, I can change it to a minute, or 5 minutes or ten minutes… That;s up to me.

Voice
It’s a scary demonstration, but that does not mean we all need to cut ourselves off from the internet immediately. The hacker in this scenario would for example need to be in wifi proximity with your phone, and hope your wifi was switched on in the first place.


Sound Up Dominic
If you think of all the ways somebody could break into your house, you’ll bankrupt yourself putting all your defenses in place. I’ve got to have an electric fence, I’ve got to have sensors everywhere, I’ve got to stick a sensor in my roof, I need to have gates in my house so that I can slow down an attacker, what if they catch me while I’m in the kitchen so I’ve got to do this.

Voice
The reality is that very few people have these kinds of hacking skills, and unless you’re a celebrity superstar or an extremely wealthy individual, hackers are probably just not going to be all that interested in you. Governments and big business on the other hand, are under constant threat.

Sound Up Angus Clarke
Right now we know that there are attacks going on within the South African network. People within other countries that are trying to hack into organizations within South Africa right now, as we speak. It happens on a daily basis, and it happens hundreds if not thousands of times on a daily basis.

Voice
Angus Clarke heads up PWC’s cyber security division – they provide security for some of the biggest private and governmental clients in the country.

Sound Up Angus
So what usually happens is that a client will contact us and say we would like to check up on the state of our security within our company.

Voice
For Angus and his team of ethical hackers, that would usually mean one of three things. The first is an external penetration test.

Sound Up Angus
Which is what we call essentially a hack of an external company’s network.

Voice
This is the typical Hollywood scenario where an outsider can remotely gain access to protected data or system functions. The second is an internal penetration test.

Sound Up Angus
Where we emulate someone within the organization

Voice
In this scenario the ethical hackers would see what damage an employee of for instance a bank, could accomplish from inside the organisation.

Sound Up Angus
Or something like for example a web application security assessment.

Voice
Which would look at the weaknesses of an institutions website and related services. But cyber criminals are not always after money. In today’s techno-centric world, governments often employ hackers to spy on both their friends and enemies.

Sound Up Dominic
I think that if we look at what came out of the Edward Snowden leaks, it’s clear that nation states are engaging in cyber in some form or another. The ones who aren’t will probably take the stuff that was leaked as a signal to probably up their capability.

Link Devi
It sounds like a Hollywood blockbuster but don’t be fooled, this is very real.

Voice
Password security for instance, can under the right circumstances, be breached. Angus showed us how this could be done using what is known as a brute force attack.

Sound Up Angus
Angus: I am going to brute force the password.

Devi: Now I feel like I’m in a movie.

Voice
In a brute force attack, hackers program software to guess your password.

Sound Up Angus
So as you can see there I’m using the user name admin, and over here on the right hand side are all the different password combinations that we are attempting.

Voice
It took the software literally 38 seconds to break the password.

Sound Up
Angus: So there we go.

Devi: What, done?

Angus: It took a couple of seconds and there is the password there.

Devi: So what was the password?

Angus: Capital Nvrgnagvuup

Voice
Don’t worry, your gmail account for example is likely safe from an attack like this – if hackers tried to brute force your password Google would throw them out after too many wrong attempts. But for every security protocol in place, a hacker somewhere is probably trying to break it.

Sound Up Angus
For hackers it’s a full time job – so where we go to work from 9 to 5, they don’t stop there. They work around the clock. And also your attackers are based all around the world. So those hacks are coming 24/7.

Voice
So it’s no wonder this is an industry worth around 4 Billion dollars in the US alone, with an estimated 2.3 million cyber security professionals employed worldwide. In a world where everything from our cars to our home appliances are connected to the net, we’re going to need them.

Link Devi
It’s called the internet of things, where devices talk to each other via an internet connection. But the more we rely on the internet, the more vulnerable we are to hacking.

Voice
So it’s probably safe to assume that ethical hacking will become a job description you’ll hear about more an more in the future. Dominic says for those of us who are worried about our cyber security, a better safe than sorry approach is the best.

Sound Up Dominic
If you are downloading movies from some dodgy website, and it asks you to install some executable, and you do and you get a virus, you could probably at this point say look you should have known better.

Voice
And here are some more tips – be wary of phishing scams where emails prompt you to click on attachments or supply private information. Never do online shopping or banking on public internet connections. And don’t be afraid to ask questions if you’re concerned.

Sound Up Dominic
So I think be wary, and be skeptical. But for the average person who has an Ipad and does most of there computing on there, you’re probably much better off than you were ten years ago when you were just doing most of it on a computer.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We meet the people on the front lines of cyber security, the ethical hackers.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: As security leaks, large scale hacking attacks and digital crimes become an ever increasing reality, governments and big business face an ongoing battle in cyber security. The need has given rise to a new kind of IT specialist - the ethical hacker. A culture born from counter culture, ethical hackers are literally paid to penetrate and exploit IT based systems.
metadata.Further information: We will be speaking to several experts in the field to get an inside look at the world of ethical hacking. To keep things interesting we will show examples of what hackers are capable of ie: hacking a person's phone and their instagram account and taking over a desktop computer and retrieving info from it, hacking a phone and switching on and recording from its camera. All of the above will be done on the experts devices with full permission from the people involved.
